cultural.vision_reason: The image shows a classic hand-woven kente cloth with strip-woven black, white, and yellow chequerboard/diamond patterning, matching the description of an Ashanti man's wrapper.

physical.title: cloth
physical.summary: Kente cloth, a rectangular man’s wrapper composed of 18 hand-woven narrow strips using black and white cotton and yellow rayon. The strips have been machine-sewn together along the selvedges. The strips are designed and arranged to form a chequerboard pattern in the central part of the cloth. Both the ends have a variant design which serves as a border to the main field; this runs continuously across the cloth. The warp in all the strips is entirely of black thread. A chequerboard pattern is created in the main field of the cloth, consisting either of diamonds in yellow against black, or of black and white stripes that alternate. The borders at the ends are entirely of small yellow diamonds against black. The warp ends have been left as a fringe.
